Query a large dataset without downloading it

Source: R/query_dataset.R
query_dataset.Rd

Opens a registered parquet dataset as a lazy table backed by DuckDB. DuckDB reads the file directly from Insper Dataverse and fetches only the columns and row groups a query needs, so large datasets such as "itbi_sp" can be filtered and summarised without loading them into memory. Use dplyr verbs to build the query and dplyr::collect() to bring the result into R.

Usage

query_dataset(dataset, ..., resource = NULL, year = NULL)

Arguments

dataset

A registered dataset alias, e.g. "iptu_sp". See list_datasets() for all aliases.

...

Must be empty. Arguments after ... must be named.

resource

The name of a logical resource within the registered dataset. When NULL, the resource marked as the default is used. See list_resources() for the available names.

year

An integer or character year used to keep a single annual file. When NULL, every annual file is included.

Value

A lazy dbplyr table (tbl_duckdb_connection) with the "doi" attribute set.

Details

Only resources distributed as parquet can be queried; use get_dataset() for the others. When a resource is split into annual files and year is NULL, all years are combined into one table.

DuckDB loads httpfs from its shared extension cache or installs it on the first call. The cache is stored under ~/.duckdb.

See also

get_dataset() to download a dataset into memory.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # live_examples() && rlang::is_installed(c("dbplyr", "duckdb"))
itbi <- query_dataset("itbi_sp")

# Transactions per year, computed by DuckDB
itbi |>
  dplyr::count(ano = dplyr::sql("year(data_de_transacao)")) |>
  dplyr::arrange(ano) |>
  dplyr::collect()
}
